text: I step off the fishing boat onto the wet Saltmarrow docks, pull my hood up against the rain, and ask the nearest dockhand what happened to the dark lighthouse.

The air in Saltmarrow tastes of salt, rot, and woodsmoke. The rain is a constant, needle-like drizzle that turns the cobblestones into slick mirrors. As your boots hit the timber of the pier, the dockhand—a man with skin like cured leather and hands stained deep with fish scales—doesn't look up immediately. He continues to haul a heavy net, his muscles straining against the weight of the sea's catch.

When he finally notices you, he pauses, his breath coming in ragged puffs of white steam. He eyes your hood, then the way you stand—like someone who hasn't spent a day hauling nets or scrubbing hulls.

"The lighthouse?" he grunts, his voice a low rasp. He leans on the wet wood, wiping a bead of water from his nose with a trembling hand. "People say the wick went out on its own. Some say the oil ran dry, but the stores were full. Others..." He pauses, glancing toward the dark silhouette of the mole and the looming grey tower beyond. "Others say the light just decided it had seen enough of the sea."

He spits into the water. "Better not go poking around the mole, stranger. The silence out there... it’s heavy. Heavier than the fog."
